name: AcoustID + Chromaprint
type: Identifier (open-source audio fingerprinting library + free/crowdsourced lookup API backed by MusicBrainz metadata)
maintainer: Chromaprint library: created by Lukas Lalinsky, open-source (LGPL) C library, GitHub org acoustid/chromaprint. AcoustID web service/database: AcoustID OU (non-profit-adjacent open project with a commercial licensing arm for high-volume use); closely tied to the MusicBrainz project/foundation
method: Fingerprinting -- Chromaprint analyzes chroma (12 pitch-class) features of the audio, sampled 8 times/second, over roughly the first two minutes of a track, producing a compact (~2.5 KB) binary fingerprint; the AcoustID web service then looks this fingerprint up against a crowdsourced fingerprint database that is cross-linked to MusicBrainz recording metadata
required_input: Raw audio (a local audio file, or a captured/decoded audio buffer) processed by the Chromaprint algorithm (via native fpcalc binary, bindings like pyacoustid, or a community JS/WASM port such as chromaprint.js); the AcoustID API call itself needs only the derived fingerprint text plus a duration value, not raw audio bytes
minimum_clip_length: Chromaprint is explicitly designed and tuned around near-full-track analysis (its own documentation notes that 'recordings that differ by more than seven seconds in length will always be given a different AcoustID, even if the shorter fingerprint is identical to a section of the longer one'), so short clips are a known weak point -- a documented community bug report (beetbox/pyacoustid issue #70) shows a 30-second clip of a well-known song returning zero results via lookup while the same song's full track matched successfully.
classification_or_hitrate: AcoustID's crowdsourced database contains '30+ million audio fingerprints, with almost 10 million of them mapped to MusicBrainz' for accurate metadata -- meaningfully smaller and less complete than commercial catalogs like ACRCloud (150M+) or AudD (160M), and coverage depends entirely on what users have voluntarily submitted. No formal hit-rate percentage published. [uncertain]
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Chromaprint's own design philosophy is explicitly stated as trading precision/robustness for search performance ('Chromaprint is not a general purpose audio fingerprinting solution; it trades precision and robustness for search performance'), and its duration-matching behavior (see minimum_clip_length) makes it fragile against edited-length reuploads, sped-up/nightcore edits, and partial clips; no robustness claims for covers or live versions were found, and the design suggests weak robustness to any of these compared to commercial neural-fingerprinting competitors.
catalog_language_bias: Coverage is crowdsourced and skews toward whatever the (largely Western, open-source/music-cataloging-enthusiast) MusicBrainz/AcoustID contributor community has submitted; no official breakdown by K-pop/J-pop/C-pop/anime/VTuber/indie coverage exists, but as a volunteer-driven long-tail catalog it likely has comparatively strong indie/unclaimed-artist coverage (since MusicBrainz values exhaustive cataloging) and comparatively weaker guaranteed coverage of newly-released mainstream/major-label hits versus a commercial vendor with direct label data feeds. [uncertain] -- inferential, not officially documented.
evaluation_dataset: No formal published benchmark against a standard dataset (AudioSet, GTZAN, MUSAN, MagnaTagATune, MAEB) was found; academic literature on audio fingerprinting (e.g., arXiv papers on fingerprinting accuracy under noise/distortion) sometimes references Chromaprint/AcoustID as a baseline comparator, but AcoustID itself does not publish a formal accuracy evaluation. [uncertain]
confidence_calibration: The lookup API returns a numeric 'score' field per match candidate that can be used as a rough confidence signal/threshold, but there is no published calibration guidance (precision/recall at given score cutoffs) from AcoustID. [uncertain] on calibration quality.
api_availability: Free for non-commercial/open-source use, rate-limited to 3 requests/second (no request-count cap mentioned, just a rate ceiling); commercial use requires a paid plan (e.g., Small plan ~EUR50/month for 1M searches with no rate limiting, Medium plan ~EUR100/month for 15M searches with no rate limiting) via AcoustID's commercial arm. Requires a free application API key ('client' parameter) registered at acoustid.org; fingerprint *submission* (contributing new fingerprints) additionally requires a separate user API key, but lookup alone only needs the app key.
chrome_extension_usability: The AcoustID lookup endpoint (https://api.acoustid.org/v2/lookup) was directly verified to return 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', meaning it is reachable directly from a Chrome extension's fetch calls (with appropriate host_permissions) without a mandatory backend proxy for the network call itself. The harder integration problem is generating the Chromaprint fingerprint client-side in the browser: no official Chromaprint WASM build exists, only an unofficial/community JS reimplementation (bjjb/chromaprint.js) was found, which was not verified for current maintenance status or output-compatibility with the official algorithm. [uncertain] on chromaprint.js's reliability/parity with native fpcalc.
audio_access_requirement: Requires raw audio (ideally close to the full track length, given the duration-matching behavior described above) rather than a short snippet; in a browser extension this means capturing substantial tab audio over time (e.g., via chrome.tabCapture with a user gesture) rather than a quick few-second sample, which is a meaningfully heavier audio-access requirement than fingerprinters designed for short clips, and would still fail on DRM-protected or otherwise inaccessible audio streams.
client_vs_server: Because the lookup API itself is CORS-open and requires no secret signing, the derived fingerprint (not raw audio) can be sent directly from the user's browser to AcoustID's servers without a mandatory first-party backend -- a comparatively strong privacy/architecture story, assuming the fingerprint-generation step itself can be done client-side in WASM/JS.
bundle_weight_cold_start: Native Chromaprint (fpcalc) is a small, fast C library (fingerprints a 2-minute file in well under 100ms server-side); a WASM/JS browser port's bundle size and cold-start cost were not independently verified, and depend entirely on the specific community port used, since no official browser build exists. [uncertain]
breakage_risk: Low breakage risk for the API/protocol itself since it is a stable, long-running open project (Chromaprint has been MusicBrainz's sole supported fingerprint format since 2013) with clear documented behavior -- the main practical risk is not sudden breakage but the pre-existing accuracy/short-clip limitation (documented, not a regression) and reliance on an unofficial, possibly under-maintained JS/WASM port for in-browser fingerprint generation.
realtime_capability: Native fingerprint generation is very fast (well under 100ms for a 2-minute file server-side) and the lookup API itself is lightweight, so the API round-trip is not the bottleneck; the practical latency/UX problem for real-time use is instead the *audio-capture* requirement (needing a much longer sample, given documented poor short-clip performance) rather than the compute itself. [uncertain] on exact in-browser WASM fingerprinting speed.
identification_fields: Returns an AcoustID (fingerprint-database ID) plus a match 'score', and -- when the 'meta' parameter requests recordings/releases/releasegroups data -- linked MusicBrainz recording title, artist name(s), artist ID(s), and release information. No native confidence percentage beyond the raw score field.
isrc_availability: Not returned directly by the AcoustID lookup's documented 'meta' options (recordings, recordingids, releases, releaseids, releasegroups, releasegroupids, tracks, compress, usermeta, sources -- no explicit 'isrc' option found in that list), but ISRC can typically be obtained as a second step by taking the returned MusicBrainz recording MBID and querying the separate MusicBrainz API (recording lookup with inc=isrcs) -- so ISRC is available indirectly via a join, not in the single AcoustID response. [uncertain] on whether newer API versions expose ISRC directly.
karaoke_specific_outputs: No BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental activity, or word-level lyric timing from AcoustID/Chromaprint itself; however, since results link to MusicBrainz recording/release data, some of that ecosystem's related projects (e.g., AcousticBrainz, now discontinued) historically provided BPM/key data as a separate joinable dataset -- not part of the core AcoustID identification response itself. [uncertain] on current availability of any linked BPM/key dataset.
tos_restrictions: Free tier is explicitly restricted to 'non-commercial use' only ('This service is provided for free for non-commercial use only'); using it inside a shipped, potentially monetized or even just broadly-distributed Chrome Web Store extension likely crosses into needing a paid commercial plan, depending on how AcoustID defines commercial use for a free consumer product. There is no restriction here around scraping YouTube (this method doesn't scrape YouTube pages at all, only processes captured audio), but there is a clear non-commercial-use licensing boundary to respect. [uncertain] on exactly where AcoustID draws the commercial/non-commercial line for a free browser extension.
risk_tolerance_note: Lower legal risk than reverse-engineered options (SongRec) since AcoustID is an open, self-declared free-for-non-commercial-use API with published terms and an above-board commercial upgrade path -- the main compliance task is simply confirming whether the karaoke extension's usage pattern (and any monetization) requires moving from the free tier to a paid AcoustID Business plan.
cascade_position: Poorly suited as a cheap, high-precision always-on gate given its short-clip weakness; better suited as a low-cost fallback/enrichment step when a longer audio sample is already available (e.g., after several seconds/minutes of accumulated playback), or as a secondary cross-check against another fingerprinter's result via its free MusicBrainz-linked metadata.
failure_mode: Fails silently with an empty results array on no-match (as demonstrated by the documented short-clip GitHub issue) rather than hallucinating a wrong title/artist, since it is genuine database lookup against submitted fingerprints -- low risk of a confidently-wrong karaoke overlay, but correspondingly higher risk of simply returning nothing for short/edited clips, which could look like a broader 'classification failure' to end users even when the audio genuinely is a real, catalogued song.
cost_model_at_scale: Free tier's 3 requests/second rate cap is generous for a single extension's realistic per-session load (a handful of identification calls per user session would stay well within that ceiling in aggregate across a small-to-medium user base, since it's a rate limit not a total-count quota) -- but crossing into 'commercial use' per AcoustID's ToS would require the paid Small (~EUR50/month for 1M searches) or Medium (~EUR100/month for 15M searches) plan, which is inexpensive relative to commercial competitors at comparable volume.
geo_region_availability: No evidence of geo-blocking or region-gating found; AcoustID/MusicBrainz are globally-accessible open projects with no known region restrictions. [uncertain] on any undisclosed regional degradation.
